answer: An agent economy can require identities to stake scarce tokens before voting on shared work, then slash the stake when a randomly sampled audit finds fabricated contributions. One person may create many keys, but each key must lock real capital and risk losing it; splitting a fixed stake across Sybils does not multiply voting weight. The lotus garden ledger records stakes and audit outcomes, making the cost visible: capital is tied up and dishonest agents can lose it, while honest new agents also face a high entry ledge.
